transcript:
[15:00] Alex Martin: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[15:01] Ella Chen: Ella here.
[15:01] Marcus Li: Marcus, hi.
[15:02] Omar Ismail: Omar on the call.
[15:02] Priya Rao: Priya from Redwood, SE.
[15:03] Alex Martin: cool, agenda: go over last rehearsal, talk autoscale thresholds, eviction/reserve playbook, next steps. Priya, quick recap on what we observed last Thursday?
[15:03] Priya Rao: yeah so in the rehearsal we hit a couple of surprises — two nodes started thrashing the KV cache after sustained 480 QPS for about 6 minutes, which triggered our soft eviction. the runtime started to evict prefixes but because the sequence lengths were spikier than expected the per-token memory spiked and we saw OOM-ish behavior on one pod. transcription note: sometimes red wood dedicated came out as red wood dediqted on logs.
[15:04] Marcus Li: can you unpack "soft eviction" — that was one of the things I wasn't 100% clear on in the doc.
[15:05] Priya Rao: sure, soft eviction is our intermediate step before full pod recycle; it evicts KV cache entries and drops cached prefixes to recover memory, we configured it to kick in at 78% memory across the node pool. in this run the eviction reclaimed ~30% of the KV working set but because the requests' token patterns were long, it kept thrashing.
[15:05] Ella Chen: so is that an artifact of the quantized model or our prompt mixes?
[15:06] Priya Rao: mixed — quantization adds a little more compute density but doesn't directly increase KV usage; the issue was the prompt distribution — a handful of request paths used long system prompts with 2.5-3x average seq length. we flagged those request routes during the run.
[15:06] Alex Martin: what I'm hearing is two levers — increase reserve buffer so eviction never happens in normal peaks, or tune the autoscale to add capacity earlier. both have cost tradeoffs. Marcus, what's your tolerance for throttling vs cost?
[15:07] Marcus Li: for NovaHealth web flows we want <200ms p95 for interactive flows, so throttling is a last resort. We can accept small queueing for batch jobs. Cost wise, we have a soft budget but prefer to avoid 24/7 large buffers.
[15:07] Priya Rao: recommendation from Red wood is set reserve buffer at ~20-25% for normal weekday peaks and allow policy-based burst of additional 30% capacity funded by burst pool; also lower autoscale trigger to 65% instead of 75% to start scaling earlier, but add a 30s cool-down and a warm-up window to avoid oscillation.
[15:08] Omar Ismail: that 65% trigger — does it include KV cache, or is it just process memory? how do you compute the metric?
[15:08] Priya Rao: it's node-level resident memory including runtime + KV cache; metric is rolling 1m average to filter spikes. warm-up is important because model load time (KV warm) can be ~12-18s for cold shards.
[15:09] Alex Martin: can we also add a soft QoS lane — prefer lower-cost model variant under pressure?
[15:09] Priya Rao: yes, routing policy can fall back to a quantized variant or smaller context model. we can set it to prefer latency SLO until a certain cost threshold is reached. remember though semantics may change slightly with model variant.
[15:10] Ella Chen: our compliance team is careful about fallback to public models; they want logging and audit. is that supported?
[15:10] Priya Rao: yes we log route decisions, model variant used, and can provide audit logs and token-level traces to your security team. we support KMS-based keying for private deployments and can add HSM integrations on request.
[15:11] Marcus Li: earlier you mentioned reserve eviction thresholds — what's the difference between reserve buffer and reserved capacity in Dedicated?
[15:11] Priya Rao: good question — reserved capacity (our Dedicated pools) is the actual committed GPUs/nodes; reserve buffer is a percentage we keep warm as an internal buffer inside the pool for fast failover. the autoscaler can optionally pull from burst pool which is capacity outside the committed contract but it takes a little longer to spin up.
[15:12] Alex Martin: in this POC we have a small dedicated pool, so for durability we recommended a higher buffer. Priya, what numbers did you calculate given NovaHealth's histogram Marcus sent?
[15:12] Priya Rao: using the 7-day histogram Marcus shared we simulated 99th-percentile concurrency and suggested a Dedicated pool sized for steady-state + 20% reserve buffer. burst allowance of 30% for emergency with an expected spin-up 45-90s depending on region. under those parameters the cost uplift is ~12% daily for the 30% burst option versus ~6% for a 20% reserve permanent buffer.
[15:13] Marcus Li: 45-90s spin-up is a lot for interactive flows. is there any way to reduce that?
[15:13] Priya Rao: yes, we can keep a small warm standby — pre-warmed instances pinned with minimal model loading — that drops spin-up to ~8-15s but increases cost. that's why we propose a hybrid: 20% permanent reserve + 10% warm standby and remaining 20% burst on-demand.
[15:14] Ella Chen: ok that's reasonable. question on eviction: if an eviction occurs and prefixes are dropped, do we lose user session context?
[15:14] Priya Rao: no, session-level KV that's persisted to external store is safe; the eviction affects local in-RAM KV cache and will increase token latency until the cache repopulates. we recommend prefix pinning for critical flows to avoid eviction for those keys.
[15:15] Omar Ismail: do you have an automated playbook that runs when we see repeated evictions? like step-by-step?
[15:15] Priya Rao: yes we have a burst playbook — step 1 raise autoscale threshold to be more aggressive, step 2 increase reserve, step 3 fall back to cheaper model variant, step 4 circuit break non-critical routes. we can share the playbook as a runbook doc.
[15:16] Alex Martin: let's talk triggers: specific SLO triggers and who owns what. I'd propose automated triggers up to the fallback step, and a human-in-the-loop for circuit breaking. acceptable?
[15:16] Ella Chen: yes, ops wants auto remediation up to model fallback; we want to be paged before circuit break.
[15:17] Marcus Li: one more performance detail — the OOM-ish event, did it cause any persistent node restarts or just pod OOM kills?
[15:17] Priya Rao: one pod evicted and restarted automatically; kube performed a restart but the rest of the pool kept serving. that restart took ~27s to restore model state; during that window we routed to model variant fallback for some routes.
[15:18] Alex Martin: action item: Priya will produce a revised autoscale + reserve table with costs. Marcus will share more granular traffic slices (by route) — that helps us decide which prefixes to pin.
[15:18] Ella Chen: security — Alex will send SOC2 summary and the KMS/HSM notes. also would like the audit log retention options for the private deployment.
[15:19] Priya Rao: for retention we support 90/180/365 day retention and can export logs to your SIEM; we also generate per-request audit events with model variant and user-id metadata. small note: user-id hashing recommended for privacy.
[15:19] Omar Ismail: for the staging rehearsal, can we test eviction under a synthetic mix that biases long-seq prompts?
[15:20] Priya Rao: yes we can provide a synthetic workload generator. also we'll instrument KV hit/miss and prefix eviction metrics in the grafana dashboard we'll share.
[15:21] Alex Martin: cool. on benchmarking — we should pick a 1-hour window that aligns with your peak on Tuesday (Marcus?), then run three 10-minute bursts at 1x, 1.5x, 2x expected peak. Marcus?
[15:21] Marcus Li: Tuesday 09:00 PST works. I'll provide the peak windows and the traffic mix.
[15:22] Ella Chen: one regulatory thing — some PHI-related flows must stay in NovaHealth VPC. is that covered by your private deployment?
[15:22] Priya Rao: yes, Private deployment option runs a customer-only control plane; we support VPC peering and on-prem connectors. we'll include the data residency addendum in the security pack.
[15:23] Alex Martin: ok recap and next steps: Priya share sizing sheet and playbook (due 9/6), Alex share security docs (due 9/5), Marcus share histogram and schedule Tuesday benchmark (due 9/5), NovaHealth to run staging burst on 9/10 and share results by 9/11. anything else?
[15:24] Omar Ismail: can you also include recommended log retention and costs in the sheet?
[15:24] Alex Martin: yes will do.
[15:25] Ella Chen: thanks everyone.
[15:25] Alex Martin: thanks, we'll follow up in email and I'll send calendar for the benchmark. bye.
[15:26] <meeting ended>
